text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Prime Minister Antonio Guterres asked fellow ministers to be more discreet after recent reported leaks in information from the government.
- Reform of the Portuguese police force is being prepared. The Communist Party is expected to support the Socialist government's proposals.

- Portuguese economy grew just under 2.5 percent in the second quarter of 1996, which indicates a light acceleration in growth since the end of 1995, according to data of the National Statistics Institute (INE).

- Prime Minister Antonio Guterres wants the government to take important decisions in the first six months of 1997. He asked ministers at yesterday's cabinet meeting to outline their priorities for the first half.

- Saudi Aramco is offering more than 2,200 escudos per share in talks to acquire a 30 to 35 percent stake in Petrogal, costing more than 60 billion escudos, a source close to the Saudis told the newspaper.

- The mayor of Oporto, Fernando Gomes, wants to clear the streets of the city of some 300 unlicensed people who help drivers park cars in return for a few escudos. These people are esimated to earn at least five billion escudos a year in Oporto, income which is not taxed.
- The cycle of falling long term interest rates in Portugal is coming to an end. The drop in the differential between long bonds and Bunds does not leave much room for further rate cuts in Portugal.
- Portuguese state airline TAP-Air Portugal chose Banque Indosuez to arrange financing for the $147 million it needs to buy 18 Airbus aircraft, Mario Matos, financial director of TAP, told the paper.
